title: How Do You Weigh an Atom? Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A kitchen scale weighs sugar in grams and a jeweller weighs gold in milligrams, but one hydrogen atom has a mass of about 1.67 × 10^-24 g. No scale could ever show that. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 1, Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry) we build a new scale just for atoms.

On the molecule bench a carbon-12 atom is split into twelve equal parts: one part is the atomic mass unit, 1 u = 1.66056 × 10^-24 g. Hydrogen balances just over one part (1.008 u) and oxygen-16 almost sixteen parts (15.995 u). Step by step we divide 1.6736 × 10^-24 g by 1 u and watch the powers of ten cancel. Then chlorine's two isotopes (34.97 u and 36.97 u, 75.5% and 24.5%) give the average atomic mass, 35.5 u, with a pause and think check. We add up methane (16.043 u) and glucose (180.162 u), watch sodium give an electron to chlorine to see why NaCl has a formula mass (58.5 u) instead of a molecular mass, then the subscript exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 8 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
